channel.description: WSJ World News RSS, without Opinions

item.title: Apple’s Biggest Battleground for Foldable Phones Is China
item.description: Huawei and other Chinese competitors reported higher demand for foldables after announcement of the iPhone Duo.

item.title: U.S. Pressure Campaign Leaves Iranian Tankers Stranded in Asian Waters
item.description: Dozens of Iranian or Iranian-linked vessels are adrift, as the U.S. threatens sanctions for countries or companies coming to their assistance.

item.title: U.K. Prime Minister Burnham Pitches an Unapologetically Socialist Makeover
item.description: The country’s new leader wants to break with recent British political history, but he must win an election first.

item.title: The Cockpit Stabbing and Terrifying Nosedive That Brought Chaos to FlyDubai Flight 1073
item.description: Passengers and crew rushed to subdue a pilot who stabbed his captain as they flew to Tel Aviv from Dubai.

item.title: Pilot-on-Pilot Stabbing Forces Emergency Landing of Israel-Bound Plane
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu described the incident as an apparent attempt to crash the plane loaded with Israeli passengers.

item.title: U.K. Says It Has ‘Strong Indications’ Iran Is Linked to Foiled Attack on Air Base
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham says Tehran played a part after five men were arrested on suspicion of plotting a terrorist act near the RAF Fairford facility.

item.title: Antisemitism Allegations Threaten French Far Right’s Efforts to Clean Up Its Image
item.description: A French news outlet reported this week that Le Pen’s fresh-faced protégé wrote antisemitic private messages more than a decade ago.

item.title: Defying Trump Has Given Carney a Popular Mandate to Transform Canada
item.description: The prime minister has high approval ratings even as he ushers in once-unthinkable changes on the environment, defense and foreign relations.

item.title: Oil Prices Rebound as Middle East Risks Persist
item.description: Oil prices rose as tensions, supply risks and shipping disruptions in the Middle East persist, even as Persian Gulf crude exports continued to recover.

item.title: Sterling Rises on Strong U.K. Data, Prospect of Fiscal Discipline And Improved EU-U.K. Ties
item.description: Sterling rose to a one-month high against the euro following upwardly revised U.K. economic growth data and after Prime Minister Andy Burnham promised fiscal discipline and improved ties with the EU.

item.title: Middle East Crude Oil Exports Back at Prewar Levels, Analysts Say
item.description: The region’s major crude producers have ramped up supplies through alternative pipelines, ports and ship-to-ship transfers to navigate disruptions due to the Iran conflict.

item.title: Inflation in Eurozone’s Biggest Economies Reaches Multiyear Highs
item.description: Enduring energy-price pressures could push European Central Bank policymakers to raise interest rates again next month.

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts for September 2026: Up to 4.50%
item.description: These are the accounts that offer the best interest rates—without burdensome fees, gimmicks or other hassles

item.title: BOE Sees Threat to Government Bonds in AI Growth Miss
item.description: A failure of AI to deliver a hoped-for acceleration in productivity and economic growth could deliver a fresh blow to prices of government bonds, the bank said.

item.title: Chilly Markets and AI Safety Debates Derail Wall Street’s Blockbuster IPO Season
item.description: Plus, the U.S. military exits Iraq, and our latest poll shows Americans want populist policies that defy traditional political labels.

item.title: North Korea Land Mines ‘Highly Likely’ Behind DMZ Explosion, Seoul Says
item.description: The blast injured three South Korean soldiers, prompting Seoul’s military to vow corresponding action if Pyongyang is the culprit.

item.title: The U.S. Military Exits Iraq, Leaving Behind a Nation in Peril
item.description: An Iraqi demand that tens of thousands of militants turn in their weapons falls short in a conflict fed by America’s war with Iran.

item.title: ‘The Blood-Dimmed Tide’ Review: Continental Ambitions
item.description: Austria-Hungary and Germany had no grand imperial vision for Central Europe beyond shaping the nationalist forces at work there.

item.title: Oil Prices Fall as Gulf Crude Exports Recover
item.description: Oil output from Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline is coming through faster than expected.

item.title: Mystery Deepens Over Alleged U.K. Terror Incident After Suspects Are Freed
item.description: The release of the five men has raised questions about the initial narrative and has left officials on both sides of the Atlantic scratching their heads.
